_comment: Copy to ~/.radar/config.json and edit. This is an explicit ALLOWLIST — radar never discovers repos by walking the disk. Secrets are NEVER stored here: tokenRef/leaderTokenRef name an environment variable, they do not hold its value.
_bridges_comment: S-004: machines whose Claude sessions radar folds in. `local: true` reads that machine's ~/.radar/events off disk instead of over HTTP. `secretRef` names the env var holding its BRIDGE_SECRET. OMIT `bridges` entirely and radar probes nothing over HTTP — it reads only this machine's own event log. See radar/HOOK-INSTALL.md.
_comment_jira: OPTIONAL (mod-jira, S-008). Omit the block entirely and sources.jira reports `disabled`. tokenRef NAMES an env var holding a Jira Data Center personal access token; the value is never stored here. Two JQL queries run per scan: open epics in `projects`, and the status of every epic key git already knows about regardless of status — the second is what makes Jira-Done-but-git-live drift detectable.
_comment_specs: OPTIONAL (mod-specs, S-009). `{}` is enough and takes the default root. Scans <root>/*/_specs/p*/ , skipping symlinks. A folder is `draft`; a specs.md carrying a GO verdict is `done`. story_list.json statuses are never read — they demonstrably lie.

repos._comment_gitBranch: `gitBranch` is OPTIONAL and only matters when dev and prod are the SAME Vercel project split by branch (app-web: main->production->app.example.com, develop->preview->app-dev.example.com). A `preview` target is multi-branch — every feature branch builds into it — so without this key the probe answers with whatever built last on ANY branch. It appends `&meta-githubCommitRef=<branch>`. Omit it when dev and prod are separate projects (site, admin, docs); absent means UNFILTERED, never a defaulted `develop`. Left unset on a non-production target, radar checks the returned deployment's branch and reports `branchMismatch` with ancestry unknown rather than guessing.
